items.title: LightManager
items.description: A project management application built around an ASP.NET Core Web API, with authentication, role-based authorization, project and task workflows, persistent PostgreSQL data and Azure deployment.
highlights: ASP.NET Core Web API with structured backend application logic
Authentication with ASP.NET Identity and JWT
Role-based project permissions and authorization
Project membership and task assignment workflows
PostgreSQL persistence through Entity Framework Core and Neon
Frontend and backend deployed separately on Microsoft Azure
items.overview: LightManager is an open-source project management application designed for small and medium-sized teams that need a straightforward way to organize projects and tasks without the complexity of enterprise project management software. The application is built around an ASP.NET Core backend and includes authentication, authorization, role-based permissions, project membership, task assignment and a Kanban workflow.
items.problem: A useful project management application requires more than CRUD operations. Users, projects, memberships, roles and tasks need to work together while the backend ensures that users can only perform operations they are authorized to perform. The goal was to build these connected workflows while keeping the product simple and easy to use.
items.solution: The application separates responsibilities between a React frontend and an ASP.NET Core Web API. ASP.NET Identity manages user identity, JWT tokens authenticate protected requests, Entity Framework Core manages relational data access and PostgreSQL stores persistent application data. Important business and authorization rules are enforced by the backend rather than depending on the frontend.

Because the application currently uses free-tier services, the backend can experience a cold start after a period of inactivity.

items.title: Price Watch
items.description: A local price monitoring system built around ASP.NET Core and Python automation. It manages products, runs scheduled price checks, validates scraped data, tracks price history, detects suspicious changes and sends email alerts.
highlights: ASP.NET Core acts as the orchestration layer between the UI and Python scraper
Python and Playwright handle browser automation and price extraction
Manual and scheduled monitoring workflows
Price validation and suspicious-change detection
Historical price tracking and dashboard visualization
Email alerts with notification deduplication
Diagnostics and failed-run metadata
Cross-process protection against overlapping scraper runs
items.overview: Price Watch is a local product price monitoring system built with React, TypeScript, ASP.NET Core, Python and Playwright. It automatically checks product prices, compares them with target prices, stores historical data, detects suspicious changes, sends email alerts and displays price trends through a local dashboard.
items.problem: Price monitoring is more than extracting a number from a webpage. A reliable system needs to know what to monitor, when checks should run, whether an extracted price is believable, whether a notification should be sent, whether the same alert has already been sent and why a particular scraper run failed.
items.solution: Price Watch separates application orchestration from browser automation. ASP.NET Core acts as the central application layer and manages products, scraper execution, email configuration and scheduling. Python and Playwright handle page loading, extraction, validation and diagnostics. The React frontend provides configuration, monitoring and historical visualization.

items.title: Developer Portfolio
items.description: A multilingual developer portfolio built with React and TypeScript to present backend-focused projects, technical writing and software development experience through a clear and maintainable application structure.
highlights: Migrated the previous portfolio approach from JavaScript to TypeScript
Multilingual content in English, Swedish and Chinese
Reusable project and article detail architecture
Responsive interface built with Tailwind CSS
Content structured around backend, APIs and AI application development
Designed for deployment through Firebase Hosting and Google Cloud
items.overview: This portfolio is a React and TypeScript application designed to present my software projects, technical experience and development direction. Rather than functioning as a simple static profile page, it uses reusable routes, multilingual content and structured project case studies.
items.problem: A developer portfolio needs to communicate more than a list of technologies. It should make technical strengths, project evidence and professional direction clear to recruiters, clients and engineering teams without becoming overly complex or visually distracting.
items.solution: The application uses React Router for independent pages, i18next for multilingual content and reusable content structures for projects and technical notes. Tailwind CSS provides a consistent visual system while the content hierarchy emphasizes backend development, APIs, automation and practical AI applications.

items.title: AI Character Chat
items.description: An experimental AI chat application combining a React and TypeScript interface with a Python service and locally hosted language models through Ollama.
highlights: Python-based AI service
Local language model integration with Ollama
React and TypeScript application interface
Separation between application UI and AI service logic
Foundation for future backend, API and persistent data features
items.overview: AI Character Chat is an experimental application exploring how locally hosted language models can be integrated into a real software application. The current version combines a React and TypeScript interface with a Python service and Ollama.
items.problem: Many AI examples stop at sending a prompt to a model and displaying the response. The goal of this project is to explore how AI functionality can become one part of a larger application architecture rather than remaining an isolated model demo.
items.solution: The application separates the frontend interface from Python-based AI logic. Ollama provides the local model runtime while the application structure leaves room for future APIs, persistent data, user state and more structured AI workflows.

features.title: Local AI
features.description: Language models run locally through Ollama instead of requiring an external hosted model API.

features.title: Separated AI Service
features.description: AI logic is kept outside the React interface to create a clearer boundary between UI and model-related functionality.

features.title: Character Interaction
features.description: The application explores conversational experiences built around AI-powered characters.

challenges.title: Application Structure
challenges.description: The project needs to remain flexible enough to grow from a simple local model integration into a more complete backend-driven AI application.

challenges.title: Model Integration
challenges.description: AI behaviour needs to be connected to application logic rather than treated as an isolated text generation endpoint.

items.deployment: The project currently uses locally hosted Ollama models and is still under active development.
learnings: Connecting application interfaces to Python AI services
Working with locally hosted language models through Ollama
Separating AI logic from frontend responsibilities
Thinking about AI as part of a larger application architecture
futureImprovements: Introduce a more complete backend API when application responsibilities justify it
Add persistent conversation and user data
